issues.item: Triggers: Family-Related Comments: Comments on family
issues.explanation: For an assault trauma, 'comments on family' is not impossible as a trigger, but paired with the rest of the profile it lacks a clear assault-linked context. The other triggers and memory items point to sensory/intrusive re-experiencing, whereas this item suggests a family-related theme not represented elsewhere in threat, appraisals, or memory.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Grief Reminders: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
issues.explanation: 'Avoid grief reminders' implies a bereavement/loss-focused coping target, but no other selected items indicate death loss or grief as a central aspect of the assault trauma. This maladaptive strategy does not fit the rest of the profile, which centers on assault-related intrusive memory, dissociation, and social avoidance.

vignette: Mr. Thomas, a 68-year-old North American male and a school counselor, has been experiencing significant distress following an assault that occurred several months ago. The traumatic event involved a violent confrontation in his home where he was physically attacked by an intruder while his wife was away on a business trip. Since the assault, Mr. Thomas has found himself overwhelmed by specific triggers that evoke vivid and distressing memories of the incident. One of the most potent triggers for Mr. Thomas is the smell of antiseptic commonly associated with hospitals or the scent of alcohol, which reminds him of the harsh environment during his ordeal. Even the mere presence of these smells can instantly transport him back to that terrifying moment. This olfactory trigger has become a significant source of distress in both his personal and professional life. For instance, whenever he visits a hospital for any routine check-ups or even encounters someone who has been drinking, Mr. Thomas feels an immediate surge of fear and anxiety. Mr. Thomas's emotional triggers are equally powerful. The thought of becoming emotionally close to others now fills him with dread due to the intense vulnerability he experienced during the assault. This aversion to intimacy has affected his relationship with his wife, as he finds it increasingly difficult to share intimate moments or express affection without feeling overwhelmed by fear. The trauma memory itself is fragmented and disjointed, often appearing in sudden flashes that bring back the same terror Mr. Thomas felt at the time of the incident. These snapshots, which consist of vivid images from the assault, emerge unexpectedly and can disrupt his daily life. He describes these memories as brief but intensely frightening moments that feel like they are happening all over again. To cope with these distressing experiences, Mr. Thomas has adopted several maladaptive strategies. One of the most prominent is dissociation; he deliberately tries to leave his body or blank out when faced with triggers or overwhelming memories. This helps him distance himself from the intensity of the trauma but often leaves him feeling disconnected and numb. The cycle of these experiences becomes increasingly apparent in Mr. Thomas's daily life. For example, at work as a school counselor, the mere prospect of emotional closeness with students can trigger his fear, leading to avoidance behaviors where he tries to keep a professional distance. This has resulted in strained relationships with some of his colleagues who have noticed his increasing isolation and reluctance to engage. Mr. Thomas's use of dissociation is not only a response to triggers but also reinforces them. Each time he dissociates as a means of coping, it inadvertently strengthens the link between these triggers and the distressing memories, making future encounters even more intense. This self-perpetuating cycle has left him feeling trapped in a pattern where his attempts to cope exacerbate his symptoms. Mr. Thomas finally sought help after realizing that his avoidance behaviors were taking a toll on both his professional life and his marriage. He was certain that his wife noticed the emotional distance he had been maintaining, which made him increasingly anxious about their relationship. What frightened him most was the prospect of continuing to live in this state of constant vigilance and isolation. In seeking therapy, Mr. Thomas hopes to regain a sense of control over his life and find healthier ways to cope with the trauma without resorting to avoidance or dissociation. He is eager to rebuild his emotional connections and return to the fulfilling role he once held as a school counselor.
